correctness.rationale: Cyclic sine interpolation and two-term determinant directly prove parity, even rank n−1 and explicit kernels. On its zero set, each determinant partial derivative is a strictly negative sine-cotangent expression, so coarea on compact angular support gives the exact positive finite 1/t tail coefficient. The inverse moment threshold and conditional error trace then follow. A facet-normal row is never orthogonal to the one-dimensional null vector; compactness bounds the augmented inverse. 1,120 finite numerical determinant comparisons and balanced cases rechecked independently, but are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Dostert–Jochemko (arXiv:2201.03419) already gives generic rank and an explicit ambiguous hexagon; Lele–Kulkarni–Willsky (1992) already gives exact sine interpolation. These known antecedents are excluded. The checked new combined claim is a full parity/nonidentifiability criterion for regular fans, a transverse singular hypersurface and sharp t^{-1} inverse-tail constant with exact moment threshold and unbounded unconditional error of the unconstrained inverse. Targeted literature and mathematical-record searches found no direct stronger implication; unindexed equivalence is a live residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed or unpublished analysis of random cyclic-bidiagonal support design conditioning could contain an equivalent inverse-tail law.

A prior general singular-matrix coarea theorem supplies the abstract mechanism; the claimed new geometry-specific calculation is the exact cyclic sine determinant, parity classification, and statistical application.
No claim is made for constrained estimators or angular laws lacking compact support.

value.rationale: One observation per cone is a natural minimal sample design for fixed-fan polygon reconstruction. The sharp odd/even distinction between merely almost-sure recoverability and nonintegrable unconditional noise risk is a substantive inverse-stability boundary, with a positive coarea constant and a simple single-facet calibration that fixes it. This is neither a rebranding of the known one-hexagon rank example nor an arbitrary finite slice.
